officials.name: Sandie Smith
officials.bio: Sandie Smith has lived most of her life in Black Hawk County, Iowa, and graduated from Waterloo Columbus High School and Hawkeye Community College. She has been employed with Black Hawk County since 1989, working in the Recorder's office, and was elected Recorder in January 2015. She is a Certified County Recorder and has implemented technology to improve public access and efficiency in her office.

officials.name: Linda Laylin
officials.bio: Linda Laylin has worked to promote economic growth in Black Hawk County for over 25 years, primarily assisting new and existing businesses with facility and employment expansions. Her additional areas of interest include capitalization of a community development fund, labor-management, and workforce development.

officials.name: Ritchie Kurtenbach
officials.bio: Ritch is a lifelong, dedicated community leader and strong advocate for working families, having dedicated decades to strengthening the local workforce and playing a key role in Iowa’s Electrical Licensing and Inspection program. As a Black Hawk County Supervisor, he brings hands-on leadership, problem-solving skills, and a commitment to public service to county government, believing in practical solutions and collaborative work.

officials.bio: Kimberly Graham is the Polk County Attorney, working to create a healthy, safer, thriving Polk County with equitable treatment in the criminal legal system. A first-generation college student, she earned her law degree from Drake University Law School in 1999 and assumed her current role on January 3, 2023, as the first woman elected to the position.

officials.name: Jamie Fitzgerald
officials.address: Administration Building 111 Court Avenue, Room 230 Des Moines, IA 50309
officials.bio: Jamie Fitzgerald has served as Polk County Auditor and Commissioner of Elections since January 2007. Fitzgerald manages a staff of 49 full-time employees in five departments. His office is responsible for a wide variety of functions, ranging from paying all of Polk County's bills to conducting elections in Iowa's largest county.

officials.name: Julie Haggerty
officials.address:
Polk County Administration Building
111 Court Avenue Suite 250
Des Moines, IA 50309
officials.bio: Julie Haggerty was sworn into office in January 2007 and is a life-long resident of Polk County. She has served the residents by establishing a same-day recording policy, launching Passport Saturdays, and actively participating in various community and county boards. Haggerty has also led efforts to digitize and preserve vital records, enhancing public access to historical documents.

officials.name: Kevin J. Schneider
officials.bio: For over 40 years, Sheriff Kevin J. Schneider has dedicated his life to public safety. Sheriff Schneider is a consummate professional, working his way through all civil service ranks from Deputy to Chief, culminating in his appointment as Polk County Sheriff in 2018, elected to a full term as Sheriff in 2020 and re-elected again in 2024. As Sheriff, Schneider leads by example in providing best practices in public safety, with an emphasis on progressive community policing and continual engagement with the community he serves.

officials.address:
Polk County Administration Building
111 Court Avenue, Room 154
Des Moines, IA 50309
officials.hours: 7:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Mon-Fri. | 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m. on the third Thursday of every month. Closed major holidays. Closed Thursday, September 17, 2026.
officials.bio: Polk County Treasurer Mary L. Wells was born and raised in Des Moines, Iowa, and holds a Bachelor of Science degree in business administration. With over 20 years in leadership positions in operations management for Fortune 100 companies, she has served as Polk County Treasurer since March 2021, focusing on customer service, online transactions, and community education. She is also dedicated to the Des Moines community, serving on several boards and as co-founder of Investing In My Future, Inc.

officials.name: Angela Connolly
officials.address: Polk County Administration Building 111 Court Avenue, Room 300 Des Moines, IA 50309
officials.bio: Angela Connolly was first elected as a Polk County Supervisor in 1998. She represents the Fifth District which includes Des Moines' North and Northwestern parts of the city, the East Village, parts of downtown, and Saylor 2. Her dedication to community engagement is portrayed through her active involvement in neighborhood organizations and civic activities, with a top priority on ensuring everyone has access to mental health services.

officials.name: Jill Altringer
officials.bio: Jill Altringer grew up in Northwest Iowa and has called Polk County home since 2001. She served on the Grimes City Council for 16 years and was appointed to the Polk County Conservation Board, serving as Chair until her election to the Polk County Board of Supervisors. With degrees in biology, chemistry, and law from the University of Iowa, Jill is dedicated to public service and enjoys outdoor activities with her family.

officials.name: Mark Holm
officials.address: 111 Court Avenue, Room 300 Des Moines, IA 50309
officials.bio: Mark Holm is a life-long Iowan who served as Ankeny's Mayor from 2022 to 2024 before being elected to the Polk County Board of Supervisors, District 3. He previously served on the Ankeny City Council for 10 years and holds a B.A. in Political Science from Iowa State University and a Certified Public Manager certification from Drake University. Mark has worked for the Iowa Department of Transportation for over 25 years and enjoys running and cycling in his spare time.

officials.name: Matt McCoy
officials.address:
111 Court Avenue, Room 300
Des Moines, IA 50309
officials.bio: Supervisor Matt McCoy represents Polk County's First District, which includes parts of Des Moines' south side and majority of the west side, Windsor Heights as well as West Des Moines and Clive within Polk County. Matt previously served two terms in the Iowa House and six terms in the Iowa Senate. He has received numerous awards for his legislative and civic participation and serves on several boards.

officials.name: Tom Hockensmith
officials.address:
111 Court Avenue, Room 300
Des Moines, IA 50309
officials.bio: Supervisor Tom Hockensmith began serving his first term in January 2003, representing Polk County’s 4th District. His previous professional experience includes roles as a policy advisor for Iowa Governor Thomas J. Vilsack, a union representative for AFSCME, and an electrician for the Iowa Department of Transportation.
